Senior Product Analyst
Location: Bengaluru, HSR Layout
Employment Type: Full-time

About AppsForBharat
At AppsForBharat, we are on a mission to assist a billion Indians in their spiritual journey and help them feel happier, more peaceful, and more content.
Our flagship product, Sri Mandir, is the world’s largest app for Hindu devotees and serves as a digital sanctuary for millions of devotees worldwide. Through Sri Mandir, users can participate in online pujas, make chadhavas (offerings), and connect with temples across India.
We are building technology-led experiences for a large and diverse user base and are looking for people who enjoy solving meaningful problems at scale.

About the Role
We are looking for a Senior Product Analyst with 4–6 years of experience in a B2C/D2C product startup or a similar high-growth environment.
In this role, you will work closely with Product, Marketing, and Engineering teams to understand user behaviour, identify product opportunities, measure product performance, and turn data into actionable recommendations.
You will go beyond reporting: using data to understand what is happening, why it is happening, and what we should do next.

What You’ll Do
• Analyse large and complex datasets to identify trends, opportunities, and areas for improvement.
• Analyse key product metrics including activation, retention, conversion, churn, engagement, and funnel performance.
• Study user journeys, behaviour, cohorts, and segments to identify opportunities to improve the product experience.
• Plan, analyse, and evaluate A/B tests and product experiments and translate results into product decisions.
• Partner closely with Product, Marketing, and Engineering teams to define problems, measure impact, and drive data-backed decisions.
• Define, track, and optimise KPIs across acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, and overall product performance.
• Identify business and product opportunities through data and provide clear, actionable recommendations to senior stakeholders.
• Support strategic planning by identifying potential challenges, opportunities, and trends.
• Conduct relevant market and competitor research to understand user needs and industry trends.
• Identify opportunities to improve analytical processes, reporting, and operational efficiency.
• Communicate complex analysis clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

What We’re Looking For
• 4–6 years of experience in Product Analytics, Product Analysis, Business Analytics, Growth Analytics, or a similar role.
• Experience working in a B2C/D2C product company or high-growth startup.
• Strong understanding of product metrics, user behaviour, customer journeys, funnels, cohorts, and retention.
• Strong SQL skills and experience working with large datasets.
• Strong proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets and experience with BI tools such as Tableau, Power BI, Looker, or similar.
• Hands-on experience with A/B testing and experimentation.
• Ability to translate data and analysis into clear, actionable product recommendations.
• Experience working closely with Product, Marketing, Engineering, or Growth teams.
• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
• High ownership and ability to work independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.
• A strong user-centric mindset and curiosity to understand why users behave the way they do.

If you enjoy solving complex problems, understanding users through data, and working closely with product teams to create measurable impact, we'd love to hear from you.

One Team. One Goal. Assisting millions on their digital devotional journeys.

71daa0932a2fbf14.description: Voice agents fail in ways traditional software doesn't. An ASR confidence drop on a regional accent misfires a tool call, an LLM hallucinates a policy because upstream latency broke turn-taking, and support teams roll these agents back within a week without anyone able to explain what went wrong. What you'll work on Evaluation frameworks. Text-only evals miss most of what matters in voice: barge-in, prosody, latency-induced errors, cross-turn context loss. You'll design audio-native metrics, generate adversarial conversational datasets across accents and edge cases, and build LLM-as-judge rubrics for task completion, empathy, and recovery from tool failures. End-to-end observability. Tracing a failed interaction means correlating audio packets, STT hypotheses, LLM reasoning traces, tool calls, and TTS output back to a single conversation ID. You'll help shape the schema and analysis layer that makes cascade failures visible across the stack. Self-improvement systems. Once you can measure and trace, the interesting work is closing the loop: mining production traces for failure patterns, generating targeted fine-tuning data or prompt updates, and validating that fixes hold under adversarial replay. Who we're looking for Someone who cares about the research questions for their own sake, and equally cares whether the work ships. Papers at Interspeech, ACL, NeurIPS, or EMNLP on speech, dialogue systems, agent evaluation, or human-AI interaction are directly relevant. Comfortable in Python, and familiar with at least one of: speech models (Whisper, Conformer variants), LLM tool-use and agent frameworks, or observability stacks (OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, Arize, Hamming). Current PhD students in ML, NLP, or speech are the robust default; exceptional MS students or research engineers with a publication track record are welcome to apply. Nice to have Prior work on evaluation methodology, dataset synthesis, or interpretability. Experience with real-time systems, telephony, or streaming pipelines. A blog, repo, or workshop paper that shows how you think in public. .
